title: Landforms and Geomorphic Processes

cards.b: Every hill, delta and dune is the result of a tug of war between forces that build land and forces that wear it down. GS I asks for this reasoning, often through Indian examples such as ravines, karst or the Sundarbans.

Endogenic forces (volcanism, folding, faulting) create relief. Exogenic forces (weathering, erosion, transport, deposition) reduce it. Landforms are the net result. Sudden endogenic events are earthquakes and volcanoes; slow ones are mountain building and warping.

Weathering breaks rock in place, with no transport. Physical (frost, exfoliation from day-night heating), chemical (oxidation, carbonation, solution) and biological types act together. Warm, wet climates favour chemical action, giving thick soils and laterite.

Mass movement is the downslope shift of material under gravity: creep, flow, slide, fall. Heavy rain, steep slopes and cut roads trigger Himalayan landslides.

Rivers cut valleys upstream and deposit downstream. Key forms: waterfalls (Jog on the Sharavati, Hogenakkal), meanders, oxbow lakes, alluvial fans where a river leaves hills, and deltas where it meets the sea. Rivers hit by a base-level fall or uplift cut deep gorges.

Ice cuts U-shaped valleys, scoops cirques, and leaves sharp arete ridges and pyramid horns (Matterhorn). It dumps moraines, and shapes drumlins and eskers. Siachen, Gangotri and Zemu are Indian glaciers. Kumaon-Garhwal glacial lakes and "hanging valleys" are common.

Wind works in dry lands: deflation hollows, mushroom rocks, yardangs, crescent barchans and fine loess deposits (China).

Groundwater in limestone makes karst: sinkholes, caves, stalactites. Waves build cliffs, stacks, spits and bars, and form beaches.

Mountains: fold (Himalaya, Alps), block or horst (Vosges, Black Forest), volcanic (Fuji), and residual or relict (Aravalli, Nilgiri). Plateaus: intermontane (Tibet), piedmont and continental (Deccan). Plains: erosional (peneplain) and depositional (Indo-Gangetic, alluvial).

The Aravalli are among the oldest fold ranges, now worn down. The Rift valley of the Narmada and Tapi is a down-faulted block, a graben.

cards.h: Davis, Penck and the cycle of erosion
cards.b:
W.M. Davis (1899) proposed a "cycle": uplift, then youth, maturity and old age ending in a flat peneplain. Walther Penck (1924) argued uplift and erosion work together, so slopes retreat in parallel.

Critics say Davis assumed a quick uplift followed by a calm period. Modern geomorphology favours dynamic equilibrium and human activity as a driver: mining, dams and farming now move more earth than many rivers.

Ravines and badlands: Chambal and Yamuna, formed by gully erosion in soft alluvium. Barchans: Thar. Karst: Meghalaya (Mawsmai and Krem Liat Prah caves), Chhattisgarh (Kutumsar) and Borra caves in Andhra Pradesh.

Delta: Ganga-Brahmaputra, the world's largest, with the Sundarbans mangroves. Coastal erosion eats Kerala's shores. Himalayan landslides, as at Joshimath (2023, subsidence), show human pressure on fragile slopes.

Likely questions

"Explain the role of running water in shaping the Indian landscape." (10 marks)

"Differentiate between weathering, erosion and mass wasting." (10 marks)

Structure: split into endogenic and exogenic; then agent by agent, with a landform and an Indian example each.

Prelims tip: know the agent behind each landform (U-valley = glacier, barchan = wind, stalactite = groundwater, oxbow = river).

quiz.q: Which is a depositional glacial landform?
quiz.w: Eskers are ridges of sand and gravel left by meltwater streams. The others are erosional.
They are crescent sand dunes in deserts like the Thar.
Dripping water leaves calcium carbonate hanging from cave roofs.
Weathering, erosion and deposition are exogenic.

quiz.q: Who proposed the cycle of erosion in 1899?
quiz.w: Davis: youth, maturity, old age; Penck later challenged the idea.
Meander loops are cut off after deposition seals the neck.

quiz.q: Ravines in the Chambal are an example of
quiz.w: Water cuts deep gullies in soft alluvium.
It is a limestone karst cave near Cherrapunji. Borra is in Andhra; Kutumsar in Chhattisgarh.

quiz.w: Fine silt carried by wind, famous in China.
